# Edgebook

Complete, editable frontend source for the Edgebook trading journal UI/UX prototype. The project uses vanilla JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and SVG charts with browser-native ES modules. There is no React/Next.js project or hidden compiled source behind this version.

**Edit `src/`.** `dist/` is generated by the build command and is excluded from Git.

## Run locally

Requires Node.js 20 or newer; Node 22 is recommended. There are no package dependencies.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/anasayub80/edgebook.git
cd edgebook
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5173**. Source changes reload the browser automatically. No environment variables, broker credentials, or API keys are required.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Serve editable source with live reload on port 5173 |
| `npm run check` | Check JavaScript syntax, module imports, and HTML entry points |
| `npm test` | Run the journal workflow and calculation checks |
| `npm run build` | Generate the deployable `dist/` directory from source |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the generated build on port 4173 |

The build copies the root HTML entry, source ES modules, styles, and public assets into `dist/`. It does not minify, transpile, or require external tooling. Static hosting should serve **`dist/`**, including its `src/` subdirectory.

## What is implemented

All ten frontend screens, shared filters, chart tooltips, CSV import/export, manual trade creation, execution summaries, trade reviews and screenshots, reflections, habits, editable playbooks, risk planning, connection drafts, settings, and JSON backup/restore.

The initial workspace contains **219 illustrative trades across three sample accounts**, dated July 20–October 16, 2026. Changes persist in this browser through `localStorage`. Entries and screenshots remain local until a backend is implemented. Reset and backup controls are available in **Settings → Data & privacy**.

## What is still to be built

The requested first phase is UI/UX. A backend, user authentication, database, MT5 EA/bridge, broker sync, detailed broker fills, live floating equity, deposits/withdrawals, server-side alerts, and live risk enforcement have **not** been implemented. The connection flow saves a local configuration draft and does not contact a broker or collect trading passwords.

The position calculator demonstrates USD-quoted instruments using a user-supplied contract size and a 0.01 lot step. Broker-specific specifications and currency conversion belong in the integration phase. Session groupings use fixed UTC windows in this preview; DST-aware templates also belong in that phase.

## Verification

Run `npm run check`, `npm test`, and `npm run build`. The workflow test covers all screens and account filters, five analytics tabs, source/time filters, empty chart samples, CSV validation, manual trade propagation, review saving, journal habits, setup creation, risk rules, connection drafts, and local backups. Browser visual QA was unavailable during this repository restructuring.
